```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# All preparation and plotting code is in this document; no external R scripts.
# Default: render from the committed small data subset.
# Rebuild: -P refresh_data:true -P raw_dir:"folder/containing/both/gzip/files"
# Download and rebuild: -P download_raw:true -P refresh_data:true
dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("output/figures", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
raw_dir <- params$raw_dir
if (isTRUE(params$download_raw)) {
  dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  base_url <- "https://data.insideairbnb.com/taiwan/northern-taiwan/taipei/2026-09-28/data/"
  for (name in c("listings.csv.gz", "calendar.csv.gz")) {
    target <- file.path(raw_dir, name)
    if (!file.exists(target)) download.file(paste0(base_url, name), target, mode = "wb")
  }
}
rebuild <- isTRUE(params$refresh_data) ||
  !all(file.exists(file.path("data/processed", c("listings_subset.csv", "audit.csv", "calendar_monthly.csv"))))
```

```{r}
#| label: prepare-real-data
#| include: false
if (rebuild) {
  dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  read_gz <- function(path) {
    # Preserve UTF-8 bytes instead of transcoding through the Windows locale.
    con <- gzfile(path, "rt")
    on.exit(close(con))
    read.csv(con, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE,
             na.strings = c("", "NA"), encoding = "UTF-8")
  }
  listings_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "listings.csv.gz")
  calendar_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "calendar.csv.gz")
  stopifnot(file.exists(listings_path), file.exists(calendar_path))
  l <- read_gz(listings_path)
  c <- read_gz(calendar_path)
  needed <- c("id", "last_scraped", "minimum_nights", "price", "room_type",
              "neighbourhood_cleansed", "accommodates", "price_quote_raw",
              "price_quote_checkin_date", "price_quote_checkout_date")
  stopifnot(all(needed %in% names(l)), all(c("listing_id", "date", "available", "minimum_nights", "maximum_nights") %in% names(c)))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(l$id), !anyDuplicated(l$id))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(c$listing_id), !anyNA(c$date),
            !anyDuplicated(c[c("listing_id", "date")]), all(c$listing_id %in% l$id),
            all(c$available %in% c("t", "f")))
  minimum <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(l$minimum_nights))
  valid_minimum <- !is.na(minimum) & minimum >= 1
  price <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub("[$,]", "", l$price)))
  currency <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(l))
  has_currency <- !is.na(l$price_quote_raw) & grepl('"currency"\\s*:', l$price_quote_raw)
  currency[has_currency] <- sub('.*"currency"\\s*:\\s*"([^"]+)".*', '\\1', l$price_quote_raw[has_currency])
  valid_price <- is.finite(price) & price > 0 & !is.na(currency) & currency == "TWD"
  group <- ifelse(!valid_minimum, NA, ifelse(minimum <= 2, "1-2 nights", ifelse(minimum <= 6, "3-6 nights", "7+ nights")))
  d <- data.frame(listing_id = l$id, last_scraped = l$last_scraped,
    minimum_nights = minimum, stay_group = group, room_type = l$room_type,
    neighbourhood_cleansed = l$neighbourhood_cleansed,
    accommodates = suppressWarnings(as.integer(l$accommodates)),
    quoted_nightly_price_twd = ifelse(valid_price, price, NA_real_),
    quote_currency = currency, quote_checkin = l$price_quote_checkin_date,
    quote_checkout = l$price_quote_checkout_date,
    quote_stay_nights = as.integer(as.Date(l$price_quote_checkout_date) - as.Date(l$price_quote_checkin_date)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  write.csv(d, "data/processed/listings_subset.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
  month <- substr(c$date, 1, 7)
  monthly <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(unique(month)), function(m) {
    z <- c[month == m, ]
    data.frame(month = m, calendar_rows = nrow(z), listings = length(unique(z$listing_id)),
      dates = length(unique(z$date)), available_rows = sum(z$available == "t"))
  }))
  write.csv(monthly, "data/processed/calendar_monthly.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  audit <- data.frame(metric = c("listings", "calendar_rows", "calendar_listings", "calendar_start", "calendar_end",
      "duplicate_listing_ids", "duplicate_listing_dates", "invalid_minimum_nights",
      "valid_positive_twd_prices", "missing_or_invalid_or_non_twd_prices", "calendar_has_price",
      "raw_listings_md5", "raw_calendar_md5"),
    value = c(nrow(l), nrow(c), length(unique(c$listing_id)), min(c$date), max(c$date), 0, 0,
      sum(!valid_minimum), sum(valid_price), sum(!valid_price), "price" %in% names(c),
      unname(tools::md5sum(listings_path)), unname(tools::md5sum(calendar_path))))
  write.csv(audit, "data/processed/audit.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(c("Calendar columns:", paste(names(c), collapse = ", "),
               "Calendar contains no date-level prices in this supplied release."), "data/processed/schema_note.txt")
  rm(l, c)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: descriptive-summaries
#| include: false
d <- read.csv("data/processed/listings_subset.csv", colClasses = c(listing_id = "character"),
              na.strings = "", encoding = "UTF-8")
levels_group <- c("1-2 nights", "3-6 nights", "7+ nights")
d$stay_group <- factor(d$stay_group, levels = levels_group)
counts <- table(d$stay_group)
good <- !is.na(d$stay_group) & is.finite(d$quoted_nightly_price_twd) & d$quoted_nightly_price_twd > 0
p <- d[good, ]
prices <- split(p$quoted_nightly_price_twd, p$stay_group)
med <- vapply(prices, median, numeric(1))
ns <- vapply(prices, length, integer(1))
stats <- data.frame(stay_group = levels_group, listings = as.integer(counts),
  share_percent = 100 * as.integer(counts) / sum(counts), valid_price_n = ns,
  median_twd = med, q1_twd = vapply(prices, quantile, numeric(1), probs = .25),
  q3_twd = vapply(prices, quantile, numeric(1), probs = .75), row.names = NULL)
write.csv(stats, "data/processed/figure_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)
colours <- c("#257F8E", "#4979AF", "#C47A35")
setup <- function() par(mar = c(4.8, 6.0, 1, 1), mgp = c(3.7, .8, 0),
                       family = "sans", col.axis = "#364457", col.lab = "#364457", las = 1)
draw_minimum <- function() {
  setup()
  at <- barplot(counts, col = colours, border = NA, ylim = c(0, max(counts) * 1.22),
          ylab = "Number of listings", xlab = "Listing-level minimum-stay requirement", axes = FALSE)
  axis(2, at = seq(0, 3500, 500), labels = fmt(seq(0, 3500, 500)), tick = FALSE)
  text(at, as.numeric(counts), labels = paste0(fmt(counts), " (", sprintf("%.1f", stats$share_percent), "%)"),
       pos = 3, cex = .95, col = "#203047")
  box(bty = "n")
}
draw_prices <- function() {
  setup()
  boxplot(prices, log = "y", col = colours, border = "#3D4855", outline = TRUE,
    pch = 16, cex = .35, ylab = "Nightly quote (TWD, log)",
    xlab = "Listing-level minimum-stay requirement", yaxt = "n", xaxt = "n")
  axis(1, at = 1:3, labels = paste0(levels_group, "\n", "n = ", fmt(ns)), tick = FALSE)
  ticks <- c(100, 300, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000, 100000, 300000, 1000000)
  ticks <- ticks[ticks >= min(p$quoted_nightly_price_twd) & ticks <= max(p$quoted_nightly_price_twd)]
  axis(2, at = ticks, labels = fmt(ticks), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = .85)
  box(bty = "l", col = "#CCD3DB")
}
for (i in 1:2) {
  png(sprintf("output/figures/figure_%d.png", i), width = 1800, height = 1050, res = 200)
  if (i == 1) draw_minimum() else draw_prices()
  dev.off()
}
audit <- read.csv("data/processed/audit.csv", colClasses = "character")
audit_value <- function(key) audit$value[match(key, audit$metric)]
valid_rule <- !is.na(d$stay_group)
valid_price <- is.finite(d$quoted_nightly_price_twd) & d$quoted_nightly_price_twd > 0
money <- function(x) format(round(x, 2), nsmall = 2, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
share <- function(i) sprintf("%.1f", stats$share_percent[i])
stopifnot(all(counts > 0), all(ns > 0), nrow(d) == as.integer(audit_value("listings")))
```

## Research question and data

Do Taipei Airbnb listings with longer minimum-night requirements exhibit smaller seasonal differences in advertised nightly prices? We hypothesize that listings targeting longer stays may maintain more stable prices. This is an observational question about association.

We use Inside Airbnb's September 28, 2026 Taipei release: **`r fmt(nrow(d))` listings** scraped September 28-29. These figures provide a first look at minimum-stay rules and quoted price levels; no model or main seasonal analysis has been run.

## Figure 1: Minimum-stay requirements

```{r}
#| label: fig-minimum-stays
#| fig-cap: "Minimum-stay groups in the Taipei snapshot. Percentages use listings with valid minimum-stay rules. Source: Inside Airbnb; team calculations."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.2
draw_minimum()
```

**What stands out.** Of `r fmt(sum(counts))` listings with valid rules, `r fmt(counts[1])` (`r share(1)`%) require 1-2 nights, `r fmt(counts[2])` (`r share(2)`%) require 3-6 nights, and `r fmt(counts[3])` (`r share(3)`%) require at least 7 nights. Requirements cluster at 1 night (`r fmt(sum(d$minimum_nights == 1, na.rm = TRUE))` listings), 2 nights (`r fmt(sum(d$minimum_nights == 2, na.rm = TRUE))`), and 30 nights (`r fmt(sum(d$minimum_nights == 30, na.rm = TRUE))`). There are `r fmt(sum(d$minimum_nights >= 28, na.rm = TRUE))` listings requiring at least 28 nights. The `r fmt(sum(!valid_rule))` listing with a missing rule is excluded.

**Why it matters.** Substantial variation in minimum stays makes it worth asking whether listings targeting different stay lengths also differ in seasonal pricing. Each proposed group contains over a thousand listings before price filtering. With date-level prices, we would compare the same listing across periods and relate its percentage price difference to these groups, accounting for neighbourhood, room type, and guest capacity. The broad 7+ group combines weekly and monthly policies, so we would also consider separating them.

\newpage

## Figure 2: Quoted nightly prices

```{r}
#| label: fig-quoted-prices
#| fig-cap: "Quoted nightly prices by minimum-stay group. Boxes show the middle half; dots lie beyond the 1.5-IQR whiskers. All eligible prices are retained on a log axis. Source: Inside Airbnb; team calculations."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.2
draw_prices()
```

**What stands out.** Among `r fmt(nrow(p))` listings with both a valid rule and a positive TWD quote, median nightly prices are **TWD `r money(med[1])`** for 1-2-night requirements, **TWD `r money(med[2])`** for 3-6 nights, and **TWD `r money(med[3])`** for 7+ nights. The 7+ group has a lower median, but the distributions overlap and include long upper tails. The log axis makes this spread visible. Of `r fmt(nrow(d))` original listings, `r fmt(sum(!valid_price))` lack a usable price and `r fmt(sum(valid_price & !valid_rule))` further listing lacks a valid rule. No otherwise eligible positive prices are trimmed.

**Why it matters.** The spread and overlap motivate a paired comparison and attention to skewness. These quotes have differing check-in dates and stay lengths, and may incorporate long-stay discounts. Differences in price levels therefore do **not** measure seasonal stability or establish that minimum stays cause price differences. A future paired analysis needs usable advertised prices for each listing in both comparison periods.

## Feasibility and next step

The supplied calendar contains **`r fmt(as.integer(audit_value("calendar_rows")))` listing-date rows** for `r fmt(as.integer(audit_value("calendar_listings")))` listings, spanning `r audit_value("calendar_start")` through `r audit_value("calendar_end")`. It contains listing ID, date, availability, and minimum/maximum nights, but **no price column**. The planned December 2026 versus August 2027 comparison cannot be calculated from these files. We must obtain date-level advertised prices or revise the question before the main analysis. Availability is not a price or a reliable booking measure; unavailable dates may be host-blocked. We will verify demand patterns before calling either month high or low season.

Inside Airbnb. (2026). *Taipei: detailed listings and calendar data, September 28, 2026 release*.
